sanskrit: yo 'sya prathamo 'pānaḥ | sā paurṇamāsī | yo 'sya dvitīyo 'pānaḥ | sāṣṭakā | yo 'sya tṛtīyo 'pānaḥ | sāmāvāsyā | yo 'sya caturtho 'pānaḥ | sā śraddhā | yo 'sya pañcamo 'pānaḥ | sā dīkṣā | yo 'sya ṣaṣṭho 'pānaḥ | sa yajñaḥ | yo 'sya saptamo 'pānaḥ | sa vaṣaṭkāraḥ | yo 'sya prathamo vyānaḥ | seyaṃ bhūmiḥ | yo 'sya dvitīyo vyānaḥ | tad antarikṣam | yo 'sya tṛtīyo vyānaḥ | sa dyauḥ | yo 'sya caturtho vyānaḥ | tāni nakṣatrāṇi | yo 'sya pañcamo vyānaḥ | ta ṛtavaḥ | yo 'sya ṣaṣṭho vyānaḥ | ta ārtavāḥ | yo 'sya saptamo vyānaḥ | sa saṃvatsaraḥ | samānaṃ arthaṃ pari yanti devā iti saṃvatsaraṃ vāvaitad ṛtavo *'nu pari yanti | yad ādityam abhi saṃ viśantīti paurṇamāsīṃ caiva tad amāvāsyāṃ cābhi saṃ viśanti | tad ekaṃ rūpam amṛtatvam eṣām ity āhutir eva | rūpaṃrūpaṃ tapasā vardhamānā ity ahorātre eva | yo 'sya dakṣiṇaḥ karṇaḥ so 'yam agnir yaḥ savyaḥ so 'yaṃ pavamānaḥ | yad asya dakṣiṇam akṣi tad asāv ādityo yat savyaṃ tad asau candramāḥ | ditiś cāditiś ca śīrṣakapāle saṃvatsaraḥ śiro 'horātre nāsike | rātryā parāṅ ahnā pratyaṅ namo vrātyāya ||
english: His first out-breath — that is the full-moon day. His second out-breath — that is the ashtakā. His third out-breath — that is the new-moon day. His fourth out-breath — that is faith. His fifth out-breath — that is the consecration. His sixth out-breath — that is the sacrifice. His seventh out-breath — that is the vaṣaṭ-cry. His first pervading-breath — that is this earth. His second pervading-breath — that is the atmosphere. His third pervading-breath — that is the sky. His fourth pervading-breath — those are the constellations. His fifth pervading-breath — those are the seasons. His sixth pervading-breath — those are the seasonal observances. His seventh pervading-breath — that is the year. 'The gods move round a common goal' — truly it is the seasons that move round the year. 'They converge upon the sun' — they converge upon both the full-moon day and the new-moon day. 'That one form is their immortality' — that is indeed the oblation. 'Growing form by form through austerity' — that is indeed day and night. His right ear — that is this Agni; his left — that is Pavamāna. His right eye — that is yonder Āditya; his left — that is yonder Moon. Diti and Aditi are the two halves of his skull; the year is his head; day and night are his nostrils. Facing west at night, facing east by day — homage to the Vrātya.

sanskrit: atisṛṣṭo apāṃ vṛṣabho atisṛṣṭā agnayo divyāḥ | rujan parirujan mṛṇan pramṛṇam mroko manohā khano nirdāha ātmadūṣis tanūdūṣiḥ ||
english: Released is the bull of the waters; released are the celestial fires — breaking, shattering all around, crushing, grinding to dust: the Mroka (corrosion), the Manohā (mind-slayer), the Khana (digger), the Nirdāha (consuming fire), the Ātmadūṣi (soul-defiler), the Tanūdūṣi (body-defiler).

sanskrit: idaṃ tān ati sṛjāmi tān mābhy ava nikṣi | tais tam abhy ati sṛjāmi yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ ||
english: I release all these away from here; let them not strike back at me. With those I release them in full force against him who hates us, against him whom we hate.

sanskrit: apām agram asi samudraṃ tvābhy ava sṛjāmi | ye 'psv agnayo 'ti tān sṛjāmi mrokaṃ khaniṃ tanūdūṣim | yo va āpo agnir āviveśa sa eṣa yad vo ghoraṃ tad etat ||
english: You are the foremost of waters; I release you toward the ocean. The fires that dwell in the waters — I release them past: the Mroka, the Khani, the Tanūdūṣi. The fire that entered your waters — that is this; whatever is terrible in you, that is it.

sanskrit: indrasyendriyeṇābhi ṣiñced ariprā āpo apa ripram asmat | praino vahatu pra duṣvapnyam ||
english: With the power of Indra, let the sin-free waters sprinkle and wash away impurity from us. Let them carry forth transgression, let them carry forth ill-dreaming.

sanskrit: śivena mā cakṣuṣā paśyatāpaḥ śivayā tanvopa spṛśata tvācaṃ me | śivān agnīn apsuṣado havāmahe mayi kṣatraṃ varca ā dhatta devīḥ ||
english: Look upon me with a benevolent eye, O Waters; touch my skin with your benevolent body. We invoke the benevolent fires that abide in the waters. O divine ones, bestow upon me sovereign power and radiance.

sanskrit: nir durarmaṇya ūrjā madhumatī vāṅ madhumatī stha | madumatīṃ vācam udeyaṃ vāco 'haṃ mā yavam | adabdho me gopā adabdho gopīthaḥ | suśrutau karṇau bhadraśrutau karṇau bhadraṃ ślokaṃ śrūyāsam | upaśrutiś ca mānuśrutiś ca mā hāsiṣṭāṃ sauparṇaṃ cakṣur ajasraṃ jyotiḥ | ṛṣīṇāṃ prastaro 'si namo daivāya prastarāya | mūrdhāhaṃ rayīṇāṃ mūrdhāhaṃ samānānāṃ bhūyāsam ||
english: Away from malice, with vigor — you are honeyed speech, you are honeyed. May I utter honeyed speech; may I not be deaf to speech. My guardian is undeceived, my protection is undeceived. May my ears be well-hearing, may my ears be auspiciously-hearing; may I hear an auspicious proclamation. May Upaśruti (Near-hearing) and Mānuśruti (Human-hearing) not abandon me — the eagle-eyed vision, the ceaseless light. You are the strewing-grass of the seers; homage to the divine strewing-grass. May I become the head of riches, may I become the head of my peers.
